conviction_note: Peer and industry prints dated after TTD last spoke (Magnite CTV +39% and a raised outlook, political ad spend at a record $11.87bn, DV programmatic activation +10%, Criteo's enterprise spend stabilising) point to Q3 clearing the >= $650m floor and give room for a Q4 guide above a bearish-looking consensus, and a 19%-of-shares short adds squeeze fuel. Against that, the stock rose 20.8% in five sessions and about 15% on the print day itself, has sold 7 of its last 8 prints, missed its own floor last quarter, and an October Evercore channel check was negative. So the findings sum to +2.0 while the scaled number stays near zero: p_up 52 on a 16% absolute move. The gap between the two is the run-up: the read-through is real, but much of it was bought on the day.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue: company guide 'at least $650m' and adj. EBITDA ~$160m (Q2 2026 release, 2026-08-06, https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260806055680/en/The-Trade-Desk-Reports-Second-Quarter-2026-Financial-Results; ppc.land https://ppc.land/trade-desk-stock-drops-24-as-q3-guidance-points-to-12-revenue-decline/). Consensus sits on the floor: Zacks $650.7m (https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/2978331/trade-desks-weak-q3-outlook-raises-concerns-whats-ahead), Benzinga $651.3m / EPS $0.22, Tiger $650.29m / EPS $0.25 (https://www.itiger.com/news/1122551591, 2026-11-02), Chartmill $656.8m / EPS $0.26, Investing.com $651m / EPS $0.25. Q3 bar sourced. The Q4 2026 bar, which is the line this name trades on, is NOT sourced: no Q4 consensus was found. The only derivation is stockanalysis.com's FY2026 revenue estimate of $2.75bn (average shown as $2.8bn, updated 2026-10-28, https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/ttd/forecast/). Less Q1 $689m, Q2 $715m and Q3 ~$651m, that implies Q4 of about $695-745m against Q4 2025's $846.8m. FY2027 is estimated at $2.60bn. Findings on the Q4 bar are capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest 83,138,457 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement (-1.1% vs 84.08m at 09-30), 19.35% of shares outstanding, days to cover 4.88 (AltIndex from Nasdaq biweekly data, https://altindex.com/ticker/ttd/short-interest; 09-30 figure corroborated by Curved Trading/FINRA via search). Short interest has been 74-89m since June. This is a crowded short. Skew_25d is +0.32 vol points, i.e. balanced (baseline priced_direction_lean 'balanced'). Put/call open interest is 0.41, call-heavy. Event-implied move 14.79% (straddle 16.2%), ATM IV 174.5%. The tape: +20.76% over 5 days, +26.93% over 20 days, about +15% intraday on 2026-11-09 before the print in a sector-wide ad-tech rally (AlphaStreet, Investing.com, 24/7 Wall St). Part of the squeeze may already have happened pre-print. The stock is 65.7% off its 52-week high, and the consensus price target is about $13.5-18, below or near spot.

findings.finding: Magnite, a sell-side platform that is a major CTV supply partner to DSPs, reported Q3 2026 on 2026-11-04, after TTD's August guide. CTV contribution ex-TAC was $105.4m, +39% y/y, against its own $98-100m guide (about +6% above the top). Total contribution ex-TAC was $200.6m against a $188-192m guide. Q4 guidance: CTV $124-127m (+33-36%), total +16-19%, and Q4 political larger than Q3. FY growth was raised to ~17% from 13-14%. That points to strong programmatic CTV demand in Q3 and into Q4, the channel TTD needs to offset soft CPG and auto brands. TTD's own bar is a ~12% y/y decline.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: TTD trades on the forward guide: the Q2 2026 guide (-12% y/y) took it -21.9%, the soft Q1 2026 guide after a Q4 beat -4.8% on the day (-16.8% pre-market), and the Q3 2025 beat -6.3%. Only 1 of the last 8 prints was up (+18.6%, May 2025).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: MGNI rose ~22% the day after its report, and TTD is +20.8% over 5 days, much of it in the same sector move. If it were fully priced, TTD's straddle would have compressed below its 13% median reaction. Instead the event-implied move is 14.8%, so the market still treats the guide as open. A sell-side beat does not prove buy-side share: Magnite also serves Amazon DSP, which Barrett did not split out.
findings.independence: Roku Q3 2026 (2026-11-02): ad revenue +23% to $727.4m, >80% of in-stream video sold programmatically, political above the 2024 presidential Q3, https://thedesk.net/2026/11/roku-q3-2026-earnings-report/. A different company and a different document.

findings.finding: AdImpact puts 2026 midterm political ad spend at a record $11.87bn, against its own prior projection of $10bn and above the 2024 presidential cycle's $11.2bn. CTV is $2.6bn (22%), more than double 2022. Magnite raised its 2026 political forecast to over $40m from $15m. TTD's Q2 call named the midterms as a boost, and its August Q3 floor was set before the overshoot was visible. Q4 carries October and early-November political spend against a Q4 2025 with none.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In 2026 this name has sold reported-quarter beats: the Q4 2025 beat fell -4.8% and the Q3 2025 beat (revenue $739m vs >= $717m guide) fell -6.3%. Political is non-recurring, and the market may discount it as one-off.
findings.why_not_priced: The aggregate is public but TTD's share is not. TTD does not disclose political, so consensus at the guide floor ($650-657m) shows no analyst has added an overshoot. If it were in the bar, Q3 consensus would sit visibly above $650m.
findings.independence: Proxy, an industry series. It shares the political component with the Magnite finding (Magnite's political raise is cited in both), so the Magnite finding is sized on CTV ex-political. Corroborated by Adweek's $11.4bn to-date and +122% CTV growth, https://www.adweek.com/convergent-tv/ctv-overtakes-cable-in-political-ad-spend-for-the-first-time-in-a-midterm/.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-16 Evercore's ad-agency channel checks were reported as negative for The Trade Desk, implying weaker near-term trends and possible share shift away from TTD (Snap also named). TTD fell 6.63% that day to about $12.20.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide is the line: -21.9% on the Q2 2026 guide. Share-loss narratives (Amazon DSP, Omnicom) have accompanied the drawdowns.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the stock fell 6.6% on the note and has since rallied about 24% from $12.20 to $15.16. That rally means the market has looked through the checks. What remains is the risk that the checks were right about Q4 agency budgets, and a 24% rebound shows the market has not kept that risk.
findings.independence: Secondhand, from an auto-generated roundup; the original note was not found. Background: AdExchanger's earlier report that Omnicom shifted Q3 spend to Amazon DSP (an older story, so not dated to 2026), https://www.adexchanger.com/platforms/omnicom-allegedly-pivoted-a-chunk-of-its-q3-spend-from-the-trade-desk-to-amazon/.

findings.finding: Amazon's Q3 2026 ad revenue was $19.6bn, +11-12% y/y, down from +26% in Q2. It missed estimates (the first ad miss in seven quarters), with the slowdown attributed to Prime Day moving into Q2. Q4 is guided to high-teens growth. Amazon DSP (renamed DVA) is TTD's main competitor, so a slower Amazon cuts both ways: less share-taking, or softer demand overall.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Amazon competition has been cited in analyst downgrades (HSBC Reduce, BNP Underperform in August 2026), not as a measured driver of a print.
findings.why_not_priced: Ambiguous in sign, so it is sized at zero. Amazon does not split out DSP revenue, so it cannot show share.

findings.finding: DoubleVerify's Q3 2026 release (2026-10-30, 8-K exhibit) shows Activation revenue, which is charged on impressions bought through programmatic DSPs and social, at $117.6m, +10% y/y. The company attributed the growth partly to 'an increase in revenue from programmatic channels'. TTD's bar is a ~12% y/y revenue decline.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Reported-quarter beats on this name have been sold (Q3 2025 -6.3%, Q4 2025 -4.8%).
findings.why_not_priced: DV suspended calls and guidance (pending sale to Nielsen at $13.60), so no previews cite it. It is a primary document, but its programmatic line pools all DSPs and social, so TTD's share of it is unknown.
findings.independence: Proxy for industry programmatic volume, independent of the Magnite and Roku documents.

findings.finding: Criteo's Q3 2026 release (2026-11-04) says spend from large enterprise performance-media clients stabilised compared with Q2. Its Q4 outlook implies contribution ex-TAC down 3-5% at constant currency against -15% in Q3, a sequential improvement in open-web brand and performance budgets going into Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide is TTD's line (see the Magnite finding).
findings.why_not_priced: Criteo is a retail and performance peer that TTD previews do not cite. The Q4 figure depends on the lapping of retail scope changes and differs between secondary sources, so it is small.
findings.independence: A different company from Magnite and DV; a proxy (Criteo sells performance media, not a DSP).

findings.finding: The 8-K item 2.05 of 2026-09-04 cuts ~15% of the workforce, substantially complete in Q3, with $39-51m of cash charges booked in Q3, partly offset by a $4-5m SBC reversal. The savings were not quantified. The Q3 adj. EBITDA guide of ~$160m (24.6% margin) was set in August, before the cut was announced. Partial-quarter savings and a run-rate opex reset give room for an adj. EBITDA beat and a firmer Q4 margin guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin compression drove part of the Q2 2026 reaction (adj. EBITDA guide ~$160m vs $241m in Q2). There is no history of TTD rewarding cost cuts, which it has not made at this scale before.
findings.why_not_priced: The charge is known and excluded from adjusted figures. If analysts had modelled the savings, adj. EBITDA consensus would sit above the $160m guide, and the Tiger preview says no margin forecast was disclosed and only RBC 'lifts forward adjusted EBITDA'. The cut came after the guide, so the guide cannot contain it.
findings.independence: The RBC note describing it as right-sizing, per https://www.itiger.com/news/1122551591 (2026-11-02).

findings.finding: Option repricing: shareholders approved it on 2026-10-19 (8-K items 5.02 and 5.07), cutting eligible employee and executive options to $12.26, that day's close. Jeff Green's Form 4 shows 1.62m options repriced from $25-74.90. In September Green received a new 7m-share performance option at $14.97 whose first tranche vests at an $18 20-day average. The vote was 441.1m for and 232.5m against, with Class B carrying 10 votes a share, so Class A holders largely opposed. The incremental SBC lands in GAAP from Q4.
findings.why_not_priced: Public in EDGAR and in the proxy. It is a retention signal, and SBC is excluded from the adjusted lines the stock trades on, so it is sized at zero.

findings.finding: Short interest is 83.1m shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, 19.35% of shares outstanding, days to cover 4.88, and has held at 74-89m since June. It is a crowded short into a print whose bar is a ~12% y/y decline, so any stabilisation in the Q4 guide forces covering.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The one up print in 8 was +18.6% (May 2025). No short-interest history at the earlier prints was checked.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly discharged: the stock rose about 15% on the print day and 20.8% over 5 days, which looks like pre-print covering. The 10-31 settlement was not found, so how much short remains at the print is unknown.
findings.independence: Curved Trading/FINRA, 84.1m at 09-30 with 2.6 DTC (via search, https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/ttd/short-interest/).

findings.finding: Run-up into the print: +20.76% over 5 sessions and +26.93% over 20, including about +15% intraday on 2026-11-09 itself (AlphaStreet: +15.2% in a sector-wide ad-tech rally), from the $12.26 repricing close on 10-19 to $15.16. That puts spot above the ~$13.5 average target. The 'low bar' thesis every preview carries was bought before the release, on a name that has fallen after 7 of its last 8 prints, including after beats.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats sold: Q3 2025 beat -6.3%, Q4 2025 beat -4.8%, Q1 2026 (beat on revenue) -1.75%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself: the question is whether the market over-bought the setup. The sealed baseline's run_up_5d_pct of 20.76% is the measurement.

findings.finding: The FY2026 consensus revenue of $2.75bn (stockanalysis, 36 analysts, updated 2026-10-28) less Q1 $689m, Q2 $715m and Q3 ~$651m implies Q4 of about $695m (-18% y/y vs $846.8m). If it is $2.8bn, about $745m. FY2027 is estimated at $2.60bn, below FY2026. Applying 2025's Q3-to-Q4 seasonal step (+14.6%) to a $651m Q3 gives about $746m, so the guide bar may sit at or below seasonal-flat.
findings.why_not_priced: No Q4 consensus is published in the wire copy, so the implied Q4 number has to be derived. It is capped small because it rests on one source whose own figures are inconsistent ($2.75bn vs a $2.8bn average).
findings.independence: none (single source; Q1/Q2 actuals from https://ppc.land/trade-desk-beat-q1-estimates-wall-street-downgraded-it-anyway/ and the Q2 release).

findings.finding: In Q2 2026 TTD missed its own floor for the first time: revenue was $715m against a guide of 'at least $750m' given in May, a $35m miss. CFO Olmstead said visibility was 'somewhat more limited', and a new CFO, CMO and CCO have since been named. So the '>= $650m' floor is less reliable as a floor than its history suggests.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: -21.9% on that miss together with the Q3 guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced; consensus sits right on the floor rather than above it, which is how this credibility discount shows up. A new finance team also tends to guide conservatively, which cuts the other way, hence the small size.

findings.finding: On 2026-11-03 TTD announced that co-founder and former CTO Dave Pickles returns to lead a new CTO Council on platform architecture, agentic capabilities and AI workflows, with no title, reporting line or start date.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None; leadership changes (new CFO, CMO and CCO) have not been tied to a print move.
findings.why_not_priced: Public and minor. It may be narrative material for the call (Kokai/agentic), but it does not land on a reported line.

baseline_tension: The skew is balanced (+0.32), so it says nothing. The findings lean positive on peer read-through and the short base, but they cut into a +20.8% five-day run-up (about +15% on the print day) that has already bought most of that read-through, on a name that has fallen after 7 of 8 prints. So p_up sits near 50 while the findings sum to about +2.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name has sold beats): Magnite read-through 1.5 -> 1.2, political 0.8 -> 0.5, DV 0.5 -> 0.3; p_up 53 -> 52
Lesson 6 (unsourced bar): the derived Q4 consensus finding is capped 1.0 -> 0.6, since it rests on one internally inconsistent source
Lesson 7 (crowded short shrinks negatives; 19% of shares out, 4.9 DTC): Evercore negative -1.0 -> -0.8, run-up negative -2.0 -> -1.5, each applied once

Left standing: restructuring as guidance (+0.5, path to the guide stated), the short-interest positive (+1.0), the Q2 floor-miss credibility item (-0.3), zeros on Amazon and the repricing, abs_move_pct 16
